albums.title: Human After All
albums.reason: With 2942 all-time plays, Daft Punk is your most-loved artist ever — and this raw, stripped-back record is the one that often gets overshadowed by Discovery. Time to let it breathe again.

albums.title: Amnesiac
albums.reason: Your 2050 all-time plays put Radiohead at number two, and Amnesiac — the dark, jazz-touched twin to Kid A — is exactly the kind of deep cut that rewards a long-overdue revisit.

albums.title: Moon Safari
albums.reason: Air sits at 1012 all-time plays and La femme d'argent and Sexy Boy are among your most-played tracks — this is the album where both live, and it's pure nostalgia fuel.

albums.title: Leftism
albums.reason: Release the Pressure is one of your all-time top tracks at 120 plays, and it lives here — Leftfield's debut is a floor-shaking masterpiece you've clearly loved for decades.

albums.title: Is This It
albums.reason: 660 all-time plays for The Strokes and you've been revisiting Room on Fire recently — so go back further to where it all started, the debut that still sounds like nothing else.

albums.title: Orbital (The Brown Album)
albums.reason: Orbital sits at 777 all-time plays and Don't Stop Me is a top-50 track for you — their debut is pure acid-house-meets-rave history and deserves a rediscovery spin.

albums.title: The Understanding
albums.reason: Röyksopp has 1062 all-time plays and tracks like The Girl and the Robot are deep in your history — The Understanding is their warmest, most song-forward record and likely hasn't had a spin in years.

albums.title: Into the Great Wide Yonder
albums.reason: With 561 all-time plays and The Last Resort already recommended, this 2010 album is Trentemøller's brooding, cinematic step forward — the one that sits right in your medium-term sweet spot.

albums.title: Overgrown
albums.reason: James Blake is your sixth most-played all-time artist and Postpone has 156 plays — Overgrown is his rich, Mercury-winning second album and a natural companion to the self-titled you've already had recommended.

albums.title: Black Sands
albums.reason: Bonobo sits at 463 all-time plays and you've been active with them over the past 12 months — Black Sands is the record that defined his sound and it fits perfectly in the recent-but-not-current vault.

albums.title: Wait for Me
albums.reason: Moby has 551 all-time plays and several albums already recommended — Wait for Me is his quietly devastating, ambient-folk record from 2009 that often gets overlooked and deserves your attention.

albums.title: Khruangbin & Maribou State
albums.reason: Maribou State has 435 all-time plays and Khruangbin has been your second most-played artist over the past 12 months — this collaborative EP sits right at the intersection of both worlds you love.

albums.title: You Make Me Real
albums.reason: You love Modeselektor's raw electronic energy and Plaid's intricate textures — Brandt Brauer Frick build techno grooves entirely from acoustic instruments, giving you something in that same cerebral-but-physical lane.

albums.title: Life Is Full of Possibilities
albums.reason: Given your deep love for Aphex Twin and early electronic introspection, Dntel's cult 2001 record — famously home to the demo that became The Postal Service — is a lost gem you'd likely adore.

albums.title: Meet Next Winter
albums.reason: Your love for Plaid and Boards of Canada-adjacent sounds points straight to Isan — this Sheffield duo made some of the most tender, melodic electronica of the early 2000s and almost nobody talks about them.

albums.title: Moondog
albums.reason: The Avalanches and your love for deeply original, timeless music with rhythmic invention makes Moondog a natural fit — the blind street musician who invented his own instruments and notation is one of music's great originals.

albums.title: We Can Create
albums.reason: Your love for Massive Attack's emotional weight and Muse's sonic grandeur points to Maps — James Chapman's debut is a swooning, Mercury-nominated record that blends electronic production with raw feeling.

albums.title: Not for Threes
albums.reason: You have 512 all-time plays for Plaid and Hawkmoth and Eyen in your all-time top 50 — but Not for Threes, their landmark 1997 album, hasn't appeared anywhere in your data and is arguably their finest hour.

albums.title: One
albums.reason: Your recent arc through Portico Quartet, Oscar Peterson, and Ill Considered shows a love for jazz with rhythmic vitality — New Zealand drummer Myele Manzanza's One has that same live, kinetic energy.

albums.title: Prize
albums.reason: Your recent listens to Alabaster Deplume and Brambles signal an appetite for music with warmth, space, and quiet originality — Rozi Plain's Prize is exactly that, a subtly brilliant album that rewards patient listening.

albums.title: Sound Sculptures Vol. 1
albums.reason: Your recent plays of St Germain, COEO, and Folamour signal a love for deep, soulful, imperfect house — Theo Parrish is the underground master of that feeling, and this collection is essential.

albums.title: On the Go
albums.reason: Your recent love for Portico Quartet, Oscar Peterson, and Charles Bradley points toward spiritual jazz with emotional depth — Manchester's Matthew Halsall is one of the UK's finest in this lane and you've somehow not landed here yet.

albums.title: Come to My Garden
albums.reason: Your deep recent engagement with Bill Withers, Syl Johnson, and Dusty Springfield shows a love for golden-era soul with depth — Minnie Riperton's 1970 masterpiece, produced by Charles Stepney, is the missing piece.

albums.title: Hypnosis Display
albums.reason: Your current explorations through O'Flynn, Dominik Eulberg, and Super Flu suggest a love for electronic music with atmosphere and feeling — Pional's debut is a beautiful, sun-faded record that sits in that warm electronic haze.

albums.title: Band of Gypsys
albums.reason: Jimi Hendrix has 41 plays in the last 7 days and you've already been through Are You Experienced, Axis, Electric Ladyland and Rainbow Bridge — Band of Gypsys is the rawer, funkier live chapter you haven't hit yet.

albums.title: Blonde
albums.reason: You've been deep in channel ORANGE this week across multiple sessions — Blonde is the natural next stop, an even more interior and atmospheric record that rewards the focused listening mood you're clearly in.

albums.title: Woman
albums.reason: Justice has 8 plays this week and you already have Planisphere in your recent albums — Woman is their lush, Moroder-indebted third album and a perfect companion to the Phantom Pt. II energy in your all-time top 50.

albums.title: War & Leisure
albums.reason: Miguel's Kaleidoscope Dream has been in your recent plays and he showed up 4 plays this past week — War & Leisure is his funkiest, most groove-locked record and a natural extension of what you're feeling right now.

albums.title: Wildflower
albums.reason: The Avalanches appeared in your last month's plays and No Bad Memories was in your recent album list — Wildflower is their long-awaited second album, a dreamy, lysergic sequel that fits the current eclectic, open-eared mood perfectly.

albums.title: Dial 'M' for Monkey
albums.reason: Bonobo has 16 plays this past month and Distance in Static is already in your recent rotation — Dial 'M' for Monkey is his earliest full-length, full of dusty, head-nodding beats that suit the relaxed current mood.

songs.title: Echoes
songs.reason: Pink Floyd sits at 1199 all-time plays for you, and this 23-minute Meddle centrepiece — one of the great deep listens in rock history — is the kind of track that rewards the long, immersive session you'd have reserved for it years ago.

songs.title: Block Rockin' Beats
songs.reason: The Chemical Brothers sit at 556 all-time plays and you've loved their albums for years — this Brit Award-winning single is pure distilled mid-90s euphoria and a deep-vault cornerstone for anyone with your electronic history.

songs.title: Unfinished Sympathy
songs.reason: Massive Attack has 535 all-time plays and multiple albums deep in your history — Unfinished Sympathy is one of the greatest British singles ever made and a track that deserves to be re-experienced at full volume.

songs.title: Two Months Off
songs.reason: Underworld has 637 all-time plays and Born Slippy is one of your top 20 tracks ever — Two Months Off from A Hundred Days Off is their later-period peak and an emotional, soaring piece of electronic music.

songs.title: Live Forever
songs.reason: Oasis sits at 617 all-time plays and this is the song that captures everything about why a generation fell for them — a pure nostalgia trigger that almost certainly hasn't had a spin in years.

songs.title: Poor Leno
songs.reason: Röyksopp is your fifth most-played all-time artist and Melody A.M. is already recommended — Poor Leno is one of the album's most emotionally resonant tracks and a deep-vault gem that hits differently after years away.

songs.title: Bad Kingdom
songs.reason: Moderat has multiple albums and tracks in the recommended history and you clearly love them — Bad Kingdom from II is arguably their defining single, moody and hypnotic, sitting right in the recent-vault era.

songs.title: Moan
songs.reason: With 561 all-time plays and The Last Resort already recommended, Moan is the track that introduced many people to Trentemøller — a perfectly constructed piece of dark minimal techno from your favourite era of his output.

songs.title: Collider
songs.reason: Jon Hopkins appears heavily in your recommended history with Immunity and Singularity — Collider is the explosive centrepiece of Immunity and one of the great electronic festival tracks of the 2010s.

songs.title: Prelude
songs.reason: Bonobo has 463 all-time plays and you've been active with him over the past 12 months — Prelude from Black Sands is a lush, string-laden piece that showcases the cinematic side of his sound and sits perfectly in the recent-vault lane.

songs.title: Locked
songs.reason: Four Tet has 26 plays in your last 12 months and Morning/Evening is already in the recommended list — Locked from that same album is a 30-minute hypnotic masterpiece and one of his most celebrated single-track releases.

songs.title: Leila Brings the Rain
songs.reason: Maribou State has 435 all-time plays and multiple Portraits-era songs recommended — Leila Brings the Rain is one of their most loved, atmospheric tracks and a perfect recent-vault return.

songs.title: Two Dots
songs.reason: Your love for Plaid's precision, Jon Hopkins' dynamics, and Rival Consoles' emotional electronica points directly to Lusine — Two Dots from the Rest of Life album is a glistening, emotional track that deserves to be in your world.

songs.title: Beams
songs.reason: Your all-time love for Orbital, Aphex Twin, and the harder edges of electronic music leads to Convextion — a deeply respected Detroit-rooted producer whose Beams is a masterclass in hypnotic, introverted electro.

songs.title: Milo
songs.reason: Given your love for Plaid, Modeselektor, and Aphex Twin's more textured moments, the Dutch duo Funckarma are a natural fit — Milo from their Funckarma 2 album is intricate, dark, and utterly distinctive.

songs.title: Cardiology
songs.reason: Your all-time love for Basement Jaxx, Massive Attack, and melodic electronic music with soul points to New Zealand producer Recloose — Cardiology is a beautiful, overlooked deep house gem with real emotional warmth.

songs.title: Lost
songs.reason: Your love for Aphex Twin's more abstract work and Modeselektor's rawness points to Actress — R.I.P. was already recommended as an album, but Lost from Hazyville is an earlier, hypnotic track that shows where it all began.

songs.title: Archangel
songs.reason: Your love for Massive Attack's atmosphere, James Blake's emotional weight, and UK bass music in general makes Burial an obvious but somehow missing piece — Archangel from Untrue is one of the most affecting electronic tracks ever made.

songs.title: Woza
songs.reason: Your recent arc through Portico Quartet, Oscar Peterson, and Ill Considered shows a love for jazz with deep feeling and space — South African pianist Nduduzo Makhathini's Woza from In the Spirit of Ntu is a profoundly moving piece.

songs.title: Meditation 1
songs.reason: Your recent heavy listening to Nils Frahm, Ólafur Arnalds, A Winged Victory for the Sullen, and Brambles shows a love for meditative, ambient beauty — Laraaji's Brian Eno-produced Meditation 1 is an otherworldly classic in that lane.

songs.title: Midnight in Peckham
songs.reason: Your recent listening to St Germain, COEO, Folamour, and O'Flynn points to a love for deep, emotional, unhurried house — New Zealand duo Chaos in the CBD made one of the decade's great deep house EPs with this track.

songs.title: Morning Matters
songs.reason: Your recent listens to Sault, Charles Bradley, and Frank Ocean signal an appetite for soulful, emotionally present music — Yazmin Lacey's Morning Matters is an intimate, beautifully understated neo-soul track that fits that feeling perfectly.

songs.title: Cure
songs.reason: Your recent love for Khruangbin's mellow grooves, Frank Ocean's introspective R&B, and Alabaster Deplume's quiet warmth makes LA trio Moonchild a natural next step — Cure is a gorgeous, unhurried piece of jazz-influenced soul.

songs.title: Summer Sun
songs.reason: Your recent engagement with Brambles, A Winged Victory for the Sullen, and Brian Eno's Apollo points to ambient music with warmth and intimacy — Amsterdam-based Jonny Nash's Summer Sun is a beautiful, hazy piece in exactly that spirit.

songs.title: Little Wing
songs.reason: You've had 41 plays of Hendrix in the last 7 days spanning multiple albums — Little Wing from Axis: Bold as Love is one of the most emotionally concentrated things he ever recorded and the perfect track for a deep listening moment.

songs.title: Pink + White
songs.reason: You've been running through channel ORANGE track by track this week — Pink + White from Blonde is one of his most universally loved songs and the natural bridge into the album that should be next in your queue.

songs.title: Audio, Video, Disco
songs.reason: Justice has 8 plays this week and Planisphere is in your recent albums — Audio, Video, Disco is their most euphoric, Daft Punk-meets-classic-rock statement and a peak-energy track that matches the Justice mood you're in.

songs.title: Le Freak
songs.reason: Chic's Everybody Dance just came up in your most recent tracks — Le Freak is the logical next move, one of Nile Rodgers' greatest creations and a track that exists on a pure feel-good frequency.

songs.title: Do You
songs.reason: Miguel showed up in your current week plays and Kaleidoscope Dream is in your recent albums — Do You from Wildheart is his most guitar-forward, Prince-influenced track and a standout that suits the eclectic mood of your current listening.

songs.title: Frontier Psychiatrist
songs.reason: The Avalanches appeared in your last month's plays and you have 511 all-time plays for them — Frontier Psychiatrist from Since I Left You is one of the most joyfully bizarre and perfectly constructed singles in electronic music history.
